title: Optimizing Telemetry Archival for Predictive Maintenance
business: A heavy machinery manufacturer monitoring thousands of IoT sensors across global fleets.
problem: Storing high-frequency sensor telemetry as row-based CSV files leads to excessive I/O overhead, as analytical queries often only require specific sensor metrics rather than the entire record set.
solution: Transitioning to the Parquet format enables columnar storage, allowing the system to read only the specific column chunks required for a query, significantly reducing data throughput.
steps: Define a schema mapping sensor IDs to individual columns to align with the columnar storage structure.
Configure the writer to group incoming telemetry streams into row groups to balance memory usage and read performance.
Serialize the data using the Parquet binary protocol, ensuring the file metadata is appended at the end of the file.
Implement a reader that parses the trailing file metadata first to locate the specific column chunks needed for analysis.
outcome: Analytical queries become significantly more efficient by skipping irrelevant data, allowing engineers to extract specific sensor trends without scanning entire datasets.
limitation: Parquet is a write-once, read-many format; updating existing records requires rewriting the entire file or creating new files, which can be verified by checking the file modification timestamps and metadata versioning.
